items.hed: The Houston Texans dominated the Indianapolis Colts 26-3 on Thursday Night Football at NRG Stadium, with C.J. Stroud throwing three touchdown passes while Indianapolis failed to score a touchdown for the first time since 2024
items.insight: Stroud threw for 194 yards and three touchdowns — to Nico Collins (42 yards), Kayson Boutte (24 yards) and Marlin Klein (13 yards) — as Houston built a 14-3 lead by early in the second quarter and never trailed again. Colts quarterback Daniel Jones threw his NFL-leading 13th interception of the season, one of two Houston takeaways off him, and kicker Spencer Shrader missed two field goals, including a 62-yard attempt blocked by Texans defensive end Logan Hall. Indianapolis played without both starting cornerbacks and both starting offensive tackles and fell to 3-8 on the season; the Colts get the weekend off before hosting the New York Giants on Nov. 29. The Texans' own schedule page shows no change to their next kickoff as of this afternoon.
items.image_caption: NRG Stadium (formerly Reliant Stadium), Houston. Venue still.

items.hed: The Astros filled out new manager Brad Ausmus's staff and general manager Randy Flores's front office this week, hiring Bobby Wilson as bench coach and Matt Bayer as an assistant general manager
items.insight: Wilson, a 43-year-old former big-league catcher who most recently served as the Washington Nationals' catching coordinator, will work under Ausmus, who takes over as Houston's manager after Joe Espada's departure. Bayer, who spent nearly 15 years in the St. Louis Cardinals' front office and rose to senior director of baseball development, joins Flores's staff as an assistant general manager, replacing Connor Huff, who resigned last week. The moves follow Houston's Nov. 12 announcement that Ausmus would return to the organization as manager, continuing an offseason overhaul of both the Astros' dugout and front office. The Astros face Monday's non-tender deadline with several arbitration-eligible roster decisions still unsettled, including right-hander Ronel Blanco, who missed most of 2026 with injury.

items.hed: The Houston Rockets fell to the Denver Nuggets 133-124 in Denver on Friday night in Emirates NBA Cup West Group A play, a rematch loss after Houston had beaten Denver earlier this month
items.insight: The Rockets dropped Friday's game at Ball Arena after winning the season's earlier meeting between the two teams, splitting the season series ahead of any further Cup or regular-season matchups, according to the NBA's own schedule and box-score pages. The loss counts in both NBA Cup West Group A standings and the regular-season column, and comes in the middle of a road-heavy stretch of Houston's schedule. The Rockets' next games are available on the league's official schedule page; Texas viewers should check the NBA's own broadcast listing rather than unofficial streams.
